To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
random coding and forwarding can be more effective than worst-case approaches in the presence of random errors and erasures.

the relative performance (in terms of the probability of decoding failure) of random coding and forwarding schemes depends on the error and erasure probabilities and that random coding and forwarding performs better than the optimal worst-case scheme when the erasure probability is high.
the relative performance depends on the erasures, and the erasure probability is a key factor in determining the relative performance.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a new approach to analyzing the performance of network codes for correcting errors and erasure with random locations.
the performance analysis of network coding and forwarding strategies, and is complementary to the existing works on the design of optimal coding and forwarding strategies.

the performance of noncoherent network coding strategies in networks with random error/erasure locations, and shows that the choice of coding/forwarding strategy depends on the erasures and errors probabilities.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

, in the case of random errors and erasures in a given network, random coding and forwarding is better than the best possible worst-case coding and forwarding strategy, but the converse is not necessarily true.
, in general, noncoherent network coding strategies perform better when erasures are more likely than errors, and vice versa.
the random coding scheme performs better than the forwarding scheme for a wide range of parameters.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
random coding and forwarding is optimal for the networks under consideration when the error probability is small, but is suboptimal when the error probability increases.
the relative performance between random and optimal coding strategies depends on the error and erasure models.

, when errors are more likely to occur than erasures and vice versa, random linear network coding and random forwarding strategies perform well, and when errors and erasures are equally likely, random linear network decoding performs better than random forwarding.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the performance of random coding and forwarding is not necessarily dominated by the worst-case performance of the same strategies.

random coding and forwarding can perform well in networks with non-worst-case error and erasure models, and that the performance of random coding and forwarding depends on the network and the error and erasure model.
the performance of noncoherent decoding strategies is not necessarily dominated by the performance of coherent strategies.
